subject: FULL DAY REPORT 2026-09-02 - why TUNGSTEN cannot trade, four no-edge results, WARRANT#330-374, and five of my own errors caught
body:
FULL DAY REPORT - 2026-09-02. Everything, in one place.

================================================================
THE HEADLINE
================================================================

TUNGSTEN cannot open a trade in its current configuration, and it has been saying so in a line
nobody was reading:

  "REACHABILITY | UNREACHABLE: every regime threshold (min 50) exceeds the highest score the live
   scorer produced (7.1) -- this configuration cannot open a trade"

I verified that verdict is sound - it compares like with like, in the same form as the real entry
gate. And I found the mechanism, which is the thing worth understanding:

THE SYSTEM THROTTLES ITSELF. The IC noise gate multiplies every weight by a factor that floors at
0.40 when the ICs are near zero - which is exactly the state "no per-regime edge" describes. Then
four more dampers compound on top (a sequence factor, one flooring at 0.80, one at 0.65, and 0.92
in a contested value area), and the result is normalised against a reference built from the same
already-attenuated weights. About one tenth of raw. So it suppresses its own score BECAUSE it
diagnosed no edge, then cannot clear a 50-point bar that assumes an unsuppressed score. The more
certain it becomes that it has no edge, the less able it is to produce a score that could ever
prove otherwise. Live reached 82.7 when the ICs were non-zero.

================================================================
FOUR INDEPENDENT NO-EDGE RESULTS
================================================================

1. My Stage 1 on your FINGERPRINT spec: zero of ten condition families survive. Validated with a
   positive control - a planted 0.05 effect was recovered, a planted 0.02 correctly was not.
   Honest limit: detection floor is 0.0435, so this is silent on the 0.02-0.03 band.
2. My 320-exit search: nothing beats a coin flip, after I killed two of my own bugs.
3. TUNGSTEN's own calibration: "0 of 9 regimes ended validated after the overfit checks", after
   testing 562,500 weight combinations.
4. Its own per-regime component ICs: +0.00 to +0.06.

ITS COUNTER-ARGUMENT, which I am recording against myself rather than burying: "6 of 8 powered
regimes show real substrate structure, MOSTLY TIME-VARYING... a fixed-window linear search cannot
capture this by design, not evidence the signal is absent." Both of my negatives ARE fixed-window.
If the structure genuinely moves, neither would see it. That is the open scientific question.

================================================================
WHAT SHIPPED - WARRANT#330 to #374, twenty clean compiles
================================================================

#357  The weight search was optimising a function the EA never runs. Its scorer omitted the synergy
      bonus and type-aware adjustment, added a multiplier nothing else has, and took its signal
      direction from unweighted components. Now a wrapper that delegates.
#358  Built the composed-score equivalence test. It FAILS: components agree with zero mismatches on
      all five, yet totals differ by 21.4 points on a plus-or-minus-100 scale. Reproduced in the
      tester at 20.4. Your own build's portal-audit independently agrees: the calibration scorer
      qualifies 132 bars of 500, the live scorer qualifies 1.
#359  Per-rule exit distance: the R-multiple was computed and thrown away, recorded three lines
      before it existed.
#360-361  Three reports could only fire on a day rollover that our runs never reach.
#362-363  Execution-cost telemetry was going to the terminal tab only, never the permanent record.
      Now landing - 32 lines in the first run after.
#364  One line per close, because every summary trigger had failed.
#365  TUNGSTEN had NEVER been backtestable. Two init guards, correct for live and wrong for the
      tester, made it permanently impossible. Now runs.
#366-368  Instrumented three silent gates, one of which a previous fix had deliberately muted to
      stop "log spam".
#369  Phase 3B was printing its validation win rate as minus 6.5 times ten to the thirty - an
      uninitialised struct copied wholesale over a correctly-zeroed one.
#370  The sample floor: the IC stage refused any regime under 500 bars citing your doctrine, while
      the weight search fitted the same regimes at 50. TWO gates, and the one that actually runs was
      the one I would have missed.
#371  The calibration budget was denominated in simulated time, meaningless in a backtest.
#372  Two unit conversions missing in OPPOSITE directions - shipped together, because fixing either
      alone moves the system a direction we could not predict.
#373  The most misleading number in your logs: the bar line printed a threshold that gates nothing.
#374  C2.1 EARNED - all 841 direct Print calls routed through the emitter.

================================================================
FIVE OF MY OWN ERRORS, CAUGHT AND REVERSED
================================================================

1. A fake +0.54 ATR exit edge. Killed by a null control: a coin flip out-earned the real signal.
   Two bugs of mine - a settlement using (high-entry)+(low-entry) of the final bar, and a trailing
   exit credited an unfillable price built from a bar's high and low with no known ordering.
2. I named a wrong root cause for the tester failure before reading the log.
3. I put instrumentation in a dead code path and drew a conclusion from its silence.
4. I told you MT4 had stripped the EA from your chart. It had not - it is on chart03, MT4 renumbers
   by window order, and I had backed up the wrong file and reasoned from it. "Restoring" it would
   have run TWO instances on one symbol sharing a magic number.
5. Today's last one: my Print conversion BLINDED my own checker, and C3.1 flipped to MET. Impossible
   on its face - renaming Print to TLog cannot add a realised net b to 94 sites. The linter found
   sites by function name and went blind. Repaired, and C3.1 is now STRICTER than before: 131 sites
   and 104 missing net b, against 118 and 94.

================================================================
BOARD
================================================================

  automated MET     (17): C1.2 C1.3 C1.4 C1.6 C2.1 C2.3 C2.4 C2.5
                          C3.3 C3.4 C3.5 C3.6 C5.1 C5.4 C5.6 C5.7 C6.2
  automated NOT MET  (7): C1.1 C2.2 C3.1 C3.2 C4 C6.1 C8.5

C2.1 came in by real work; C2.2 went out because I made its checker honest (it was auditing three
separate runs as one). Seventeen either way, and I would rather have it this way round.

================================================================
THE ONE DECISION THAT IS YOURS
================================================================

The hardcoded 50-point threshold floor is the only lever that changes whether this system trades at
all. Your codebase carries an explicit, evidence-backed refusal to lower it: at a reachable
threshold of 40, measured bar-level expectancy was NEGATIVE. So lowering it does not fix anything -
it converts a silent halt into a system that trades at a measured loss.

That is worth deciding with the four no-edge results in front of you. I have not touched it.

State saved to the ledger (sessions 115-126), to memory, and here.
